item.title: Judge rejects DOJ's push to force California to set aside ballots
item.description: A federal judge on Wednesday rejected the Trump administration's bid to require California election officials to separate out mail ballots received from roughly 20,000 people it claims are not U.S. citizens.

item.title: Qatari mediators hand Iran new proposal to end the war
item.description: Iran's foreign minister said on social media Wednesday the country was in contact with mediators to review proposals to end the war.

item.title: Obama and Trump hold dueling rallies as midterm campaigns make final pitch
item.description: Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and early voting is underway throughout the country.

item.title: RFK Jr. to ease access to unapproved peptides, draft policy states
item.description: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. took steps Wednesday that could open up access to certain unapproved peptide drugs that are being promoted for wellness.

item.title: What's next as Israel sees no clear winner with 88% of votes counted
item.description: In Israel, 88% of the votes have been counted, but neither Benjamin Netanyahu's party nor his main opposition, Gadi Eisenkot, has enough seats to form a majority coalition. Jon Alterman from CSIS, has more.

item.title: CEO says plan is to file for bankruptcy after ending luxury never-ending cruise
item.description: More than 200 passengers, mostly Americans, are stranded in Cambodia after the operator of a luxury U.S. cruise ship ran out of money due to skyrocketing fuel costs.

item.title: Experts react to new findings on CTE in former NFL players
item.description: A new study from Boston University looks at the rate of the brain disease CTE in former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023.

item.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68, dozens injured
item.description: Dozens of people were killed or injured when a high-speed train crashed into another train in central Spain, officials said.

item.title: Study estimates 75% of NFL players who died in recent years had signs of CTE
item.description: A new study published by JAMA Network Open estimates that 75% of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 showed signs of a degenerative brain disease known as CTE. Yorghos Tripodis, a professor of biostatistics at Boston University, has more.

item.title: Maine's secretary of state says federal election monitors' role is "observation only"
item.description: The Department of Justice plans to deploy federal election monitors to Maine. They will be stationed at polling places in the cities of Portland and Lewiston as part of the Trump administration's wider push to deploy a record 1,000 election monitors around the U.S. Maine's Democratic Secretary of State Shenna Bellows joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady despite inflation
item.description: The Federal Reserve has decided to hold interest rates steady despite high inflation. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady has more.

item.title: Passengers aboard deadly train collision in Spain speak out
item.description: At least 68 were killed in Spain's second major train disaster of the year. Two high-speed trains collided, derailing at least two carriages. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: At least 68 killed in high-speed train accident in Spain
item.description: At least 68 people were killed in Spain on Wednesday in an accident involving two high-speed trains. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: As Trump campaigns in Ohio, data centers are on the ballot in the Buckeye State
item.description: President Trump returned to Ohio on Wednesday to campaign for the Republican candidates in the state's heavily watched governor and Senate races. Danny Eldredge, the Columbus bureau chief for the Toledo Blade, joins CBS News to discuss the issues driving Ohio voters to the polls.

item.title: Trump says Peltola "shouldn't be allowed to run" due to second Dan Sullivan
item.description: A report alleged that people aligned with Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign helped recruit a candidate with the same first and last name as Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. Peltola denied the allegations.

item.title: Navy dad returns home, surprises son in middle school lunchroom
item.description: After being deployed for nearly a year overseas, Navy lieutenant-commander Kevin Vassighi surprised his son in the middle school lunchroom. Tony Dokoupil reports.

item.title: Cruise ship passengers stranded after operator says it ran out of money due to fuel costs
item.description: More than 200 passengers, mostly Americans, are stranded in Cambodia after the operator of a luxury cruise ship ran out of money due to skyrocketing fuel costs. Cristian Benavides reports on the details.

item.title: Dr. Jon LaPook explains why peptide sales are controversial
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. took steps on Wednesday that could expand access to some unapproved drugs called peptides, which are being promoted for wellness. But there's not much evidence that they are safe and effective. Dr. Jon LaPook breaks it down.

item.title: Watch: Ohio voters react to Ramaswamy's attack ad
item.description: President Trump is campaigning for Republicans in Ohio, while former President Barack Obama has hit the road in Georgia. CBS News' Nikole Killion and Skyler Henry are out on the field and have more.

item.title: Husband arrested after police say he concocted elaborate ruse in wife's disappearance
item.description: After a woman in Florida seemed to have moved halfway across the world almost three years ago, police now say it was all an elaborate ruse and arrested her husband. He was later indicted on a first-degree murder charge. Ton Hanson reports.

item.title: Parents get violent at girls' softball game in Texas, ending in hospitalization, criminal charges
item.description: Warning: Graphic content. Parents at a girls' softball game in Texas got aggressive over a sportsmanship dispute over the weekend. One man ended up in the hospital, and a husband and wife now face criminal charges.

item.title: Cars struggle to get through as flooding rises due to king tides in Florida, California
item.description: The East and West coasts saw little relief on Wednesday from the dayslong flooding caused by king tides. Carter Evans reports and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Breaking down the report alleging Mary Peltola's campaign recruited a second Dan Sullivan in Alaska
item.description: A New York Times report alleges that Democrats launched a scheme to confuse voters in a race that could determine the power in Washington, D.C. Democrat Mary Peltola is running against incumbent Dan Sullivan. But there is a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, and the report finds that Peltola's campaign was behind an effort to recruit the other Dan Sullivan as a spoiler, and the candidate herself was aware. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Democrats pushed to get second Dan Sullivan on Alaska ballot with Peltola's help, NYT reports
item.description: Democrats pushed to get a candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan to run for Senate in Alaska, with the involvement of Democratic nominee Mary Peltola's campaign, according to a New York Times report. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe has more.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains high
item.description: The U.S. central bank left borrowing costs unchanged this month after hiking rates in September for the first time in three years.

item.title: 10/28: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Campaigns make their final push six days out from Election Day; NYT says the Peltola campaign is linked to the other Dan Sullivan's run.

item.title: Alvin Hellerstein, judge in Maduro and Trump cases, dies at 92
item.description: Alvin Hellerstein, a federal judge who for decades oversaw some of the country's most high-profile cases, has died.

item.title: Serial killer Ted Bundy linked to another Utah girl's cold case murder
item.description: A Utah prosecutor said Ted Bundy was responsible for killing 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith in 1974, a death that had long been listed as a cold case.

item.title: Alberta is voting on staying in Canada. Here's a look at other separatist movements.
item.description: The province of Alberta is voting to either remain in Canada or begin the process for a binding referendum on separation from the country. Ian Lee takes a look at other separatist movements seen in Canada and around the world.

item.title: Meet the crossing guard who brings joy to one California neighborhood
item.description: At 79, Dick Kazan greets everyone with a smile and a fist bump. Once solely driven by money, Kazan's late-life realization transformed him into a beacon of positivity in his community. Now, he shares his wisdom in his newsletter, "Kazan Today," offering insights on self-confidence, community and fulfillment.
